instructions: At least 6 hours ahead, or the night before: bring about 5 cups of water and the 2 tbsp vinegar to a boil in a medium pot over high heat.
Lower the 6 eggs into the water one at a time with a spoon. Turn the heat to medium so it bubbles gently, and cook for 6 minutes for a soft, jammy yolk. This makes 6 eggs, enough for 3 people.
Meanwhile, fill a bowl with ice and cold water. Transfer the eggs into it with a slotted spoon and leave them for about 10 minutes, until completely cold.
Finely chop 1/4 of the onion, mince the 3 garlic cloves and slice the scallion.
In an airtight container big enough to hold the eggs, stir together the onion, garlic, scallion, 10 tbsp soy sauce, 5 tbsp honey, 1/4 cup water and the sesame seeds until the honey dissolves.
Peel the eggs gently and add them to the container. If they float, press a piece of plastic wrap onto the surface so the eggs stay under the marinade.
Close the container and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
Halve the eggs and spoon some of the marinade over them. Serve cold. Keep the rest in the marinade in the fridge for up to 1 week, best within 3 to 4 days.
advance_prep_notes: marinate at least 6 hours ahead, or overnight
method_notes: Two Plaid Aprons and Take Two Eggs both soft-boil large eggs for 6 minutes, chill them in ice water and marinate in soy, honey, garlic, onion, scallion and sesame for at least 6 hours. Two Plaid Aprons uses more soy to honey and a little water, and Take Two Eggs adds a second chili, which is left out here to keep the base mild. The lead's chili is optional and skipped. Running to the Kitchen uses hard-boiled eggs with a shorter 2 hour marinade.
